body:
The pinned DSH MCP HTTP transport follows cross-origin redirects and can forward MCP session IDs and business tool arguments outside the configured platform origin.

## Confirmed scope

- Plugin: `@openbkn/dsh-business-context@0.2.0-rc.2-openbkn.0.2.0-13`; official DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`.
- Call path: bkn-dsh `OpenBknMcpManager.mountFiber` -> DSH `dsh-mcp-client` -> `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0` `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` -> native fetch.
- bkn-dsh supplies an explicit Bearer header and checks the initial MCP URL's origin. DSH does not configure a redirect-denying fetch. The initial URL check does not cover automatically followed Location responses.
- Controlled localhost probes with the actual SDK passed under Node 22.22.3, Node 24.21.0 and the official macOS Desktop Electron 44.0.0 / Node 24.18.1 runtime. Cross-origin 301/302/303 retained the MCP session ID; 307/308 also forwarded the tools/call body, including a synthetic bkn_start_interaction question. Authorization was stripped in all tested runtimes.
- The current platform's initialize/tools-list requests returned 200 without redirects. A session-ID-only read without Bearer returned 401. No real leakage or authentication bypass was observed, and no live business call was used for the security probe.
- The vulnerable code belongs to the upstream MCP SDK and is used by DSH. This is not the OpenBKN CLI/SDK login implementation. The mount/auth source path is unchanged from plugin -10.

## Upstream tracking

- [GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw): confirmed reachable HTTP redirect exposure; patched MCP client version is 2.3.0.
- [GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h): the current plugin mount does not configure SDK OAuth providers, withOAuth or direct auth/fetchToken calls. A controlled 401 stopped without OAuth discovery/token exchange. Retain this distinction when reviewing future host changes.

## Release disposition

On 2026-10-24, maintainer @kalias explicitly accepted this existing host risk for the unchanged -13 release and requested follow-up in the bkn-dsh 0.3.0 project. The risk is retained in the -13 release notes. This issue does not claim either upstream advisory has been fixed.

Do not modify or republish the already accepted -13 package as part of this tracking item.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Select and document a reviewed host/transport remediation that prevents cross-origin forwarding without silently changing the supported host contract.
- [ ] Cover cross-origin 301/302/303/307/308 with synthetic credentials, session IDs and business arguments; prove the second origin receives no protected request.
- [ ] Preserve supported same-origin behavior, normal MCP calls, CLI-managed authentication and explicit 401 handling.
- [ ] Recheck the OAuth advisory if a future integration introduces SDK OAuth providers.
- [ ] Verify the resulting candidate on the affected Desktop and npm/Web host paths, with Windows coverage scoped to the changed boundary.
- [ ] Record artifact identity, actual host versions and limitations before closing.

Source references: [plugin mount](https://github.com/openbkn-ai/bkn-dsh/blob/c947287f9cabe4416d969e213c83f3e56d5c7344/packages/openbkn-business-context/src/openbkn-mcp-manager.ts#L107), [pinned DSH transport](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/transport.ts#L31).
title: security: harden the DSH MCP transport against cross-origin redirects
